questions.prompt: Explain how the LMS learner route tests run the real Express router without a server: what is imported and what is mocked (and when), how the dispatch helper and response recorder work, what this executes and what it skips, how the transaction argument is represented and what the assertions check about it, and what the audit/event spies and the Prisma lookup fixtures can and cannot stand in for.

keyPoints.text: The fixture imports the actual Express router, with Vitest hoisting mocks for Prisma, authentication, events and audit before that import.
keyPoints.quote: Vitest hoists mocks for Prisma, authentication, events and audit before that import.

keyPoints.text: A dispatch helper builds method, url, headers, body, query and params and calls router.handle; the recorder resolves on json and next captures errors.
keyPoints.quote: Its response recorder resolves a promise on json; the next callback captures errors.

keyPoints.text: This runs the real handler guards and branches without opening a port or running production JWT parsing.
keyPoints.quote: without opening a network port or running production JWT parsing.

keyPoints.text: The transaction argument is a Proxy distinct from the default Prisma object, forwarding the same delegate methods.
keyPoints.quote: The transaction argument is a Proxy distinct from the default Prisma object

keyPoints.text: Assertions verify that completion passes that callback client to the audit and event helpers.
keyPoints.quote: Assertions verify that completion passes this callback client to audit and event helpers.

keyPoints.text: Those helpers are spies, so the suite neither inserts DomainEvent/OutboxMessage rows nor proves SQL rollback.
keyPoints.quote: the test does not execute actual DomainEvent/OutboxMessage insertion or prove SQL rollback.

keyPoints.text: The scope-aware findUnique checks ID, actor and organization, but the findFirst fixture is not a complete database query engine.
keyPoints.quote: is not a complete database query engine.

questions.prompt: What does the LMS route suite's mocked transaction prove, and what can it not prove? Explain how $transaction is faked, which two things the assertions do establish, why rollback is out of reach, how the guide proposes to prove rollback (setup, injected failure, assertions, and the status of that sketch), why db push rather than migrate deploy is used, and which operational claims neither a compile nor a mocked request supports.

keyPoints.text: The fake prisma's $transaction just runs the callback with a Proxy over the same object.
keyPoints.quote: whose `$transaction` simply runs the callback with a `Proxy` over the same object.

keyPoints.text: It proves the route uses the transaction client for every write, by counting calls on testState.tx.
keyPoints.quote: That proves the route *uses* the transaction client for every write

keyPoints.text: With the failing-commit test, it also proves a failed transaction is not reported as success.
keyPoints.quote: a failed transaction is not reported as success.

keyPoints.text: It cannot prove PostgreSQL discarded the enrollment, lesson progress and domain event together; a fake has nothing to roll back.
keyPoints.quote: a fake has nothing to roll back.

keyPoints.text: To prove rollback, run one integration test against a disposable database, with a trigger that raises on DomainEvent insert, and assert enrollment and lessonProgress counts are zero.
keyPoints.quote: To prove the rollback, write one integration test against a disposable database.

keyPoints.text: That test is only a sketch: neither the file nor the dispatchAgainst helper exists yet.
keyPoints.quote: neither the file nor the `dispatchAgainst` helper exists yet.

keyPoints.text: There is no prisma/migrations directory, so migrate deploy would apply nothing and db push is used instead.
keyPoints.quote: The repo has no `prisma/migrations` directory, so `migrate deploy` would apply nothing.

keyPoints.text: Neither a compile nor a mocked request establishes PostgreSQL availability, Redis delivery, browser interaction or certificate PDF generation.
keyPoints.quote: Neither a successful compile nor mocked request establishes PostgreSQL availability, Redis delivery, browser interaction or certificate PDF generation.

questions.prompt: How does the LMS testing guide tell you to debug a failing learner request and read the suite's evidence? Explain what a 403, a 409 completion result and the 500 for the malformed stored score each mean, what to check for a successful mutation, why zero transactions is not automatically a failure (and how the terminal guard test shows it), and how many cases the suite has now versus the recorded run and what the web and worker scripts contribute.

keyPoints.text: Debug by identifying the request's first failing boundary; a 403 means tenant membership failed.
keyPoints.quote: A 403 means tenant membership failed.

keyPoints.text: A 409 completion result means the required work did not qualify.
keyPoints.quote: A 409 completion result means the required work did not qualify.

keyPoints.text: A 500 for the deliberately malformed stored score is an internal configuration failure.
keyPoints.quote: A 500 for the deliberately malformed stored score is an internal configuration failure.

keyPoints.text: For a successful mutation, check the transaction and side-effect arguments as well as the response.
keyPoints.quote: check the transaction and side-effect arguments as well as the response.

keyPoints.text: A no-op or terminal request legitimately has zero transactions.
keyPoints.quote: A no-op or terminal request legitimately has zero transactions; zero is not automatically a failure.

keyPoints.text: The terminal guard case starts from an already-completed enrollment and proves no new transaction or event is requested, without first completing and reloading.
keyPoints.quote: proves that no new transaction or event is requested.

keyPoints.text: The suite now has 31 cases (15 + 1 API, 15 domain), but the recorded run predates the two newest learner cases and reports 29; web and worker scripts use --passWithNoTests and contribute zero.
keyPoints.quote: Web and worker test scripts use `--passWithNoTests` and contribute zero cases.
